claims.text: WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args) returns a WebApplicationBuilder, the object an app registers its services and configuration on.

claims.text: Calling builder.Build() produces the WebApplication object, and its Run() call starts the app listening (on Kestrel).
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, Fundamentals: WebApplication and minimal hosting

claims.text: The order in which builder.Services.Add... calls run does not affect how any individual request is later handled.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, Dependency injection fundamentals (service registration order)

claims.text: app.MapControllers() scans controller classes and registers a method-and-path pair (an endpoint) for each attribute-routed action method.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, Routing: Endpoint routing / MapControllers

claims.text: A controller action method's body runs once per matching request, not when app.MapControllers() itself executes at startup.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, Routing: Endpoint routing

claims.text: In DonHang.Api/Program.cs, AddControllers() is what lets app.MapControllers() later find and register the project's controller classes.
In DonHang.Api/Program.cs, builder.Build() is on line 52 and app.Run() is the file's last line, with database-migration and request-pipeline wiring code between them.
GET /api/v1/products against the running lab returns the product list on repeated calls, computed by the controller method each time, not cached from startup.
